Jess (Acme): Hey team — we're seeing intermittent errors from the embeddings endpoint. In our pipeline some calls error out with 'embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 768'. Happens when we reuse a cached prefix vector for repeated documents. Request ID: r-id-9a7c2, sample time: 2025-10-30T14:22:11Z. Any quick ideas?
Sara - Support: Sorry you're hitting this, @Jess. Can you paste the exact request payload and the model name you're calling? Also are you mixing multiple embedding models in the same process?
Jess (Acme): We think it's the same model but our app does on-the-fly model switching for A/B tests. Example request we used: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"embed-open-1536","input":"/docs/faq#question123|user-prefix:42","cache":true}'``` We also have older workers that used `embed-compact-768` months ago.
Cal - Platform: Thanks, that helps. Quick note: our embedding cache keys should include model id + normalized input + options, but I'll check if deprecated cache keys might still be around. Can you also include a raw log snippet (the service side logs show cache GET/HIT/MISS)?
Jess (Acme): Paste from our end (truncated): ```ERROR embedding_pipeline: dimension_mismatch expected=1536 got=768 key=sha1:/docs/faq#question123|user-prefix:42 cached_model=embed-compact-768 request_model=embed-open-1536```
Sara - Support: OK that looks like a classic cache key collision where a cached vector from a different model variant was returned. Two suspects: 1) keys historically didn't include the model string for very old cache entries, 2) our CDN/edge layer had a normalization bug with '|' and '#' characters in keys. Tagging @Cal - Platform and @Mina - Oncall to confirm.
Cal - Platform: Reproduced locally. Admin cache lookup showed a HIT returning a 768-dim vector for a key that should've included model but didn't because an old migration created keys hashed only on the normalized text. The short version: older cache entries created before the 'model in key' fix can collide.
Mina - Oncall: Immediate mitigation: 1) we've purged keys matching the customer's prefix hash from the internal cache (done at 14:45 UTC). 2) We can force the API to bypass cache per-request by honoring `cache=false` (not advertised publicly but available). 3) We're preparing a small compatibility job to backfill and re-key old entries.
Jess (Acme): Thanks — after the purge we're seeing far fewer errors. Is there a recommended client-side change to avoid this in future?
Sara - Support: Short-term: ensure you lock the model for your entire pipeline (don't mix embed models on the same document keys). Longer-term: we'll roll a server-side fix so model id + embedding options (pooling/truncation) are always part of the cache key.
Cal - Platform: Action items: INF-1029 created to rekey legacy cache entries and harden key generation (includes model id, truncation, and 'input_normalizer' salt). Hotfix branch is up, will deploy canary to staging tonight and to prod tomorrow morning (2025-10-31).
DeployBot: Deployment INF-1029/hardening started (canary) at 2025-10-30T22:00:12Z.
Mina - Oncall: Note on billing/throughput: some customers saw small throughput spikes after purge because more embedding calls fell through to compute. We monitored and CPU/GPU utilization stayed within expected delta; no billing anomalies detected yet but flagged growth to finance.
Jess (Acme): Agree, we saw a temporary throughput jump. Everything stabilized after the purge. Really appreciate the quick turnaround.
Sara - Support: Follow-ups: we'll keep the job to re-key old entries in priority queue. Please avoid switching model ids in the same pool until INF-1029 is live. I'll email the release notes and the workaround (cache=false) to your account and mark the ticket as high priority. :thumbsup:
Jess (Acme): Sounds good. Can you notify when ledger shows no more dimension_mismatch errors for our org?
Cal - Platform: Will do, I'll add a short alert rule to watch the error counter for your org and ping in this thread when it's zero for 24h.
Jess (Acme): Thanks everyone, resolving on our side for now. :relieved:
